answer: Admission uses a public reverse auction for a fixed number of credentials each epoch. Every candidate posts a 100-credit bond and a sealed work bid; the contract selects the 64 cheapest valid bids, then samples five signed tasks over 14 days. A signal beacon randomizes tasks, a ledge checkpoint fixes deadlines, and a thread nullifier prevents proof reuse. One credential can earn at most 60 credits, so each extra fake identity risks at least 40 credits plus independent task work; missed or copied proofs burn 80%, and all bids, proofs, and slashes are auditable.
